frequency_question: How often does an administration successfully publish a final rule for a massive, highly contested regulatory fee increase within a single presidential year window?
membership_rule: Includes economically significant fee-schedule or cost-imposition rules proposed by federal agencies that faced intense initial legal or industry pushback; excludes routine annual fee adjustments or minor procedural updates.
provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 named; captures the specific class of high-salience, aggressive executive fee and immigration rule finalizations.
known_gaps: Excludes rules withdrawn prior to finalization due to sudden political shifts.
skeleton: 3 major contested high-impact immigration/fee rulemakings finalized under past tight executive push within equivalent timeframes, out of 3 major attempts identified.
validity_reason: Base rate tied to executive rulemaking velocity under standard administrative procedure acts and holds until presidential term transitions.
